base: 6.3.0 (v63.json): everything not listed here is unchanged
split: product = (1) mechanics + electronics-case holder [6.x], (2) detachable electronics module [case 1.x]: the mechanics can be printed now
frame: as 6.3: Z-up mm, shaft axis x=y=0, Z=0 = bowl base underside, LOCKED bayonet pose

decisions.servo: stays in the chassis (coaxial cradle, structural). OWN SEALED BAY: scatola_v64 is the 6.3 box cut down to the cradle width; sealed by the cap lip on its rim, the tower face O-ring, the shaft O-rings, an O-ring under P2, the M12 gland and an ePTFE vent patch. Flood fill: one closed volume (119 cm3 free) separate from the module, the pod and outside
decisions.module_removal: achieved: from BELOW, unit hanging or taken down, WITHOUT opening the chassis: 2 screws (hex 2.5) + 1 M8 plug. Not tool-free: a tool-free latch would also open for a fox
decisions.panel_side: the panel moves with the electronics from the room side (button at 77 deg, under the release button) to the side away from the bowl: the button now faces 16 deg, i.e. 60 deg clockwise from the release button seen from above. The room side is blocked by the servo body (the servo cannot be turned: P2 would fall under it)
decisions.envelope: not feasible in this pod: the bay wall is at x 15.25 and the skin 59-65 from the axis, so the depth is 35-43 on the centre line and falls to 25-33 at y +-34; width 68 between the guides (99 across the front lobes), height 61
decisions.second_board: slot B is real but shares the depth: with the ESP32 stack at 25 mm the board in slot A fills the depth in front of it, so a second FULL board only fits when the stack in A is <= 6.0 mm (regulator board in A, ESP board on low sockets in B: [np.float64(12.8), np.float64(19.2)] mm in front of B). The 6 V / 5 V regulators and the capacitor fit beside / under the ESP stack and in the lobes (demo layout)
decisions.pod_seam_oring: dropped: the opening crosses the cap / shell seam, and nothing in the pod needs the pod to be sealed any more (bay and module are sealed on their own); the pod stays closed (gaps <= 0.4 mm) with its drain

branch_12v.part: 2-core PUR (or the pigtail of an M8 4-pin A-coded male field connector) to the pod-top M8 IP67 pair

access.note: take the 2 lock screws out, let the module down: at 80 mm its top is 13 mm below the pod bottom and the plug ring is free in the hand; unscrew the ring and set the module on the bench. Refit: plug, lay the loop on the lid between the back fence and the turret, push up

servo_lead_pass_through.where: M12x1.5 gland (IP68, cable range 3-6.5 mm) in the bay south wall at x -3.0, z -48.0 (the 6.3 gland position)
servo_lead_pass_through.solution: the servo lead does NOT pass the gland. A ROUND 3-core cable (the harness servo branch, PUR 3 x 0.25 mm2, Ø4.0) goes through the gland, which seals on it as designed; inside the bay it is terminated with a JR/Futaba 3-pin female (crimped after passing the gland) and the servo plugs into it in the dry south room of the bay (mated pair parked vertically at x -5..2.6, y -31..-27.4). The servo and its flat lead stay untouched and replaceable; no new printed part
servo_lead_pass_through.crimp_connector: JR/Futaba-style 3-pin servo housing, female, 2.54 mm pitch + 3 female crimp terminals for 22-26 AWG (servo-lead type); pin order: signal (orange/white) - +6 V (red) - GND (brown/black); crimp with an open-barrel crimper (e.g. Engineer PA-09)
servo_lead_pass_through.order: pass the stripped round cable through the dome nut, seal insert and gland body from outside, crimp and insert the 3 terminals, tighten the dome nut (2.5 N m), plug the servo; then fit the cap

inherited_from_6_3_0 (parts and outer en.why: bowl, flange plates, gate blade and ring, disc, plates, chute, latch, button are the 6.3.0 files; the shell keeps its outer skin, tabs, button boss and top edge, and the module fills the opening flush

gate_open_passage.note: 6.3.0: the opening apex is pulled back to r 4.6 round the dowel seat (-17.3 mm2, inside the narrow tip no kibble passes); the largest inscribed circle is unchanged

gate_hold.assumptions: full 200 L drum (Ø585 x 850 mm kibble), bulk density 0.45, wall friction 0.3 (kibble on HDPE), Janssen K 0.4; design pressure = max(2 x Janssen at the bottom, Janssen asymptote, hydrostatic without wall friction)
gate_hold.blade_model: PETG plate 3.0 mm, simply supported over the largest inscribed circle of the opening (Ø44.0); the blade rests on the lower plate all round the pie (and on the landing floor past the far edge at full stroke)
gate_hold.creep: long-term stress < 1 MPa: no creep concern
gate_hold.closing: single-bevel knife leading edge (0.6 edge, 25 deg) lifts pieces into the column; over-travel 12.4 deg past the far edge into a landing whose far end has a 1.6 mm drain slot (crumbs fall out, no crumb cake); torque at the ring ~0.1-0.5 N m

inherited_from_6_3_0 (parts and outer en.drainage: drain 1 and floor screed as 6.3; drain 2 (the +X sump) is gone with the sump: the module stands there

print.modulo_guarnizione_v64: TPU, base on the bed, lip up; Arachne walls, 15 mm/s (the 0.8 mm lip prints as one line)

open_risks: panel no longer on the room side (see decisions.panel_side): if that matters more than the module depth, the alternative is a module without the panel plus a panel left in the cap
second full board only with a low ESP stack; the 80 x 60 x 45 target is not reachable in this pod
J1: M8 5-pin is a 3 A connector; fine for a standard servo, not for a high-torque one
lid: 5 screws; the back edge and the two notch edges (~105 mm) have no screw and rely on the ribbed 3.2 mm lid and the soft outward lip. Water test before trusting IP66
guscio_v64 needs tree supports under the inner part of the 3 bowl tabs
J1 socket and its nut size are assumed, verify on the bought part before printing the lid
PT screws in the lid bosses: ~5-10 openings; for a development module melt M3 inserts into the 5 bosses (Ø7.5) instead
speakers Ø26-28 need the tall ring and a board notch
KO3 is shallow (guide wall behind it)
pod seams are 0.35 mm gaps without a seal: dust and insects are stopped by the ribs only; everything behind them is sealed or drains
the module weighs on two M3 inserts in printed posts (SF 4.8 at 250 N); do not hang anything from the module
